key_insight: Natural language processing of EHR symptom notes uncovered distinct motor neuron disease subgroups beyond onset-site labels, with symptom patterns linked to different survival outcomes.
clinical_relevance: This approach could improve phenotype definition, prognostication, and identification of patients who may need tailored supportive care based on symptom burden.
method: Used MedCAT NLP to extract symptom mentions from clinical notes in 2,361 confirmed MND patients.
Filtered concepts to UMLS symptom/sign terms and removed negated mentions.
Clustered binary symptom profiles with latent class analysis and compared survival across clusters.
evidence_signal: The study found four clusters in first notes and three clusters in all notes, with significant survival differences across clusters (log-rank p < 0.001).
watch_item: Results come from a single tertiary center and depend on clinical-note quality, so external validation and careful implementation are needed before use in routine care.
paper_title: Symptom-based phenotype discovery in motor neuron disease using natural language processing of electronic health records
